title: Microburst priming retro — standup notes
content:
Meeting: ad-hoc perf sync (microburst priming retro) — 2026-10-12
Attendees: Aisha, Luca, Mei, Omar, Priya, + oncall (Jon) briefly
Duration: 45m
Location: #eng-perf and Zoom

Purpose: capture observations from last week's odd microburst tail-latency episodes, compare priming/warmup strategies across canary hosts, and lock down immediate mitigations before the holiday traffic spike.

Quick summary:
- Regressions observed on canary cluster after kernel/allocator tweak KALLOC-37 rolled on 2026-10-06: intermittent p99 spikes (3–6x) for short bursts (1–3s) across mixed-sequence traffic. Average latency and throughput largely unchanged.
- Heatmap playback confirms bursts line up with sudden sequence-length mix shifts (many short prompts followed by long continuations) and certain model variants with larger KV working sets (13B+).
- Two strong hypotheses: (A) priming/warmup path creates transient KV cache churn causing high stall percentages on the GPU-side dispatcher; (B) new allocator increases fragmentation under alternating small/large allocation patterns.

Evidence and notes from runs:
- Replay used: playback-job-2026-10-09-v3 (5x faster than production sampling), dataset = customer-simulated-churn-100k.
- Typical metrics from run windows where spike occurs:
  - baseline host: qps ~ 160, p50 18ms, p95 46ms, p99 220ms
  - affected host: qps ~ 155, p50 20ms, p95 50ms, p99 1.2s (spike windows)
  - GPU stall % (perf counters) during spikes: 48% vs baseline 12%
  - KV-cache hit-rate dip from 91% -> 63% coincident with spike windows
- Flamegraphs show short-lived CPU-side scheduling stalls in the dispatcher thread at the point of swapping KV segments. Stack traces point at kv_cache::evict_hot_segment + allocator::free_slab.
- Microbench to isolate allocator: ran allocator-fuzz-io workloads on patched and previous kernel images. With KALLOC-37 present, small-allocation churn (random 64B–512B) 3x slower and shows higher fragmentation counters.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Priming churn: when warmup sequences run with model variants that allocate larger KV segments, the async priming writes into the KV cache concurrently with user-facing requests leading to lock contention and eviction cascades. Evidence: spike correlation with warmup jobs and KV hit-rate dips.
2) Allocator fragmentation: KALLOC-37 changed free-list ordering causing delayed reclamation of slabs used by small control structures (scheduling queues). Evidence: allocator microbench regressions and increased free-list length in counters.
3) Scheduling backpressure: bursty arrival of short requests forces dispatcher to re-prioritize and triggers large copy ops; combined with (1) or (2) this amplifies tail.

Immediate mitigations tested in lab (results):
- Disable async priming on canary: p99 reduced from 1.2s -> 280ms in spike windows, KV hit-rate stabilised ~88%. (test branch: disable-async-priming-2026-10-10)
- Pin allocator to previous kernel build at host-level (rollback KALLOC-37): p99 restored to baseline (230–260ms) but observed slight throughput dip (~3%).
- Rate-limit warmup jobs with token-slice throttle (new scheduler flag warmup_max_qps=10): reduced overlap windows, p99 ~300ms, complexity: warmup completion time increased by ~40%.

Tradeoffs discussed:
- Rolling back KALLOC-37 reduces latency but may reintroduce memory-safety improvements from the patch. Need security/infra signoff to keep rollback long-term.
- Disabling async priming reduces tail but could increase cold-start latency for rarely used KV segments — affects outlier serving for low-traffic tenants.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Aisha: open a security-scoped rollback RFC for KALLOC-37 rollback on canaries and limited hosts; target: 2026-10-14. Linked to RWD-4821.
- Luca: instrument kv cache eviction to add a short-lived metric (evict-burst-count) and hook into console alerting; target: 2026-10-15. (PR: /pull/2219 ref)
- Mei: prototype a cooperative priming mode (throttled priming with backpressure awareness) and run on staging; target: 2026-10-18. (branch: cooperative-priming)
- Omar: run allocator microbench matrix across 3 kernel variants and produce reproducible perf artifacts (perf.data + flamegraphs) and upload to confluence; target: 2026-10-16. Ticket RWD-4834.
- Priya: coordinate a limited canary rollout that disables async priming during peak window (midnight UTC) for 48h and capture traces; target: schedule by 2026-10-17.
- Oncall (Jon): set a temporary alert: if p99 > 600ms and KV hit-rate drops > 20% relative baseline, page the perf team.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there tenants with extremely skewed sequence-length distributions that trigger this more often? Need per-tenant heatmap slice. (Priya to request from billing + routing team).
- Can we make priming idempotent and cooperative (skip if eviction pressure > threshold)? Mei to spike.
- Long-term: should priming be moved to separate CPU-bound worker pool to avoid interfering with dispatcher? Pros/cons and infra cost must be estimated.

Notes to self / scratches from meeting:
- Consider adding a per-host priming budget metric (priming_tokens_in_flight) to use in routing policies.
- Remember to check GC-related syscalls latency during spike windows (munmap/madvise patterns looked suspicious in earlier trace).
- Possible quick patch: add jitter to priming start times so they don't align with peak user windows (low-effort, low-risk).

Meeting artifacts / links:
- Playback job: s3://perf-playback/2026-10-09-v3/trace.tar.gz
- PR for disable async priming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2219
- Allocator microbench results: confluence/perf/allocator-matrix-2026-10-11

Next sync: short follow-up on 2026-10-15 10:30 PT to triage initial artifacts and decide on rollback plan.

End notes: this doc is a working capture — please add inline comments here or drop notes in #eng-perf. Will convert to a formal retro if rollback or major config changes are approved.
